proposition.claim:
Definition 2.5 calls the finite-field obstruction absent if, over every finite residue field \(k\) of the base and every finite extension \(k'/k\), the number of \(k'\)-points of the source does not exceed that of the target. Lemma 2.6 states that a finite \(k\)-scheme \(Y\) embeds as a closed subscheme of a nonempty open \(V\subset\mathbb A_k^1\) if and only if this condition holds and \(Y\) is a closed subscheme of some smooth \(k\)-curve [CF, p. 8]. The first sentence of its proof on page 9 uses this condition to choose an embedding of the closed point of a connected \(Y\). The actual page images confirm this wording.

k=F2. Y=SpecF4 finite and connected. Y is closed in smooth connected C=A1_F2 via t²+t+1. V=D(t²+t+1) nonempty open of A1_F2. for every finite extension F_{2^m}, count Y=2 if even/0 odd; countV=2^m−2 if even/2^m odd; all inequalities hold.
